title: FloodGuard planning protocol v1a: decision rules
status_note: Draft written by an AI coding agent for the owners' signature. Agents draft, humans sign. Nothing in this file is in force. It takes effect only when both signers have filled the signature block, every entry in drafter_readings is marked confirmed or amended, the file is committed, and the SHA-256 of the committed file is recorded in docs/proposal_execution/RECEIPTS.jsonl. No receipt has been written.
drafted_by: AI coding agent (Claude), on the owner go-ahead R5 of 2026-10-01
purpose: Declare, before any planning-tier FPPS, A-E class or ensemble is computed, the rules that turn a flood input into planning outputs: evidence tiers and lanes, the confidence rule, the scoring frame, the class rules, the guardrails, the cases and what the team had already seen when it chose these rules. Outputs are planning guidance. They are not official warnings and not real-time detection.

scope.covers: Planning outputs only (the additive planning overlay). Plan row G7a.
does_not_cover: The accepted lane: accepted_fpps and accepted_action_class stay null and tier T4 stays locked.
The nine SHA-bound finals modules listed in scripts/build_mae_sai_finals.py, which are not edited.

Engineering parameters (corridor polygon, grade joins, closure parameters, facility sets, critical links, national anchors, ensemble grid, scenario and engine grid, class rule v2 inputs). Those are in planning_protocol_v1b.json.

lanes.name: Observed evidence
lanes.definition: An event-aligned or self-dated observation: a flood input with one acquisition date that is within +/-3 days of the case reference date.
may_claim: What the dated input shows on its date, described as an own unqualified candidate (T2) or as an agency extent used as provided and unvalidated (T3).
A binding A-D class only at T3 with derived medium confidence, or at T2 when the declared skill condition passes.
may_not_claim: A validated, qualified or accurate flood map.
That the 22 Oct layer describes the September event.
Any class above E for a row whose temporal_relation is not event_aligned.

lanes.name: Scenario
lanes.definition: A declared perturbation or assumption applied to a real base case, including assumed completions (T1 assumed-completion arithmetic).
may_claim: What the classes would be under the named assumption, labelled as scenario classes.
may_not_claim: An observed outcome. Scenario classes are counted only in the SCN column and are never merged with observed classes.

lanes.name: 2024 season-envelope scenario
lanes.definition: The UNOSAT/GISTDA product 4009 accumulated layer treated as if every area ever mapped flooded in the season were flooded at once. A scenario, part of the SCN column.
lanes.display_text: 2024 season envelope scenario: all roads ever mapped flooded treated as closed at once
may_claim: Scenario classes under the season envelope, with the standard 4009 sentence and CC BY-SA 4.0 attribution.
may_not_claim: An observation of any day or of the September event.
A dated extent: the layer has no per-patch dates and Field_Validation=0.

lanes.name: Engine test
lanes.definition: Synthetic fixture or boundary grid. Not a place.
may_claim: That the engine reproduces every class and the 0-100 bounds.
may_not_claim: Anything about a real place. Engine classes are never counted as an observed or scenario distribution.

tiers.name: Engine test
tiers.display: Grey chip: Engine test, not a place. Studio engine tab and appendix only.

tiers.name: Scenario
tiers.admission: Real context plus a declared perturbation or assumption, including SCN-ENV (4009 season union treated as simultaneous) and assumed completions.
tiers.max_confidence: scenario confidence: rule v1 with the recency condition replaced by the scenario declaration. How condition C1 applies to a T1 row is not stated in the plan; see confidence_rule_v1.scenario_rows.
tiers.class_behaviour: Scenario classes, never merged with observed and counted only in the SCN column.

tiers.name: Own candidate
tiers.admission: A FloodGuard output: M1-literal, M1-v2, the UN-SPIDER reproduction, the A6-prime classifier; the legacy 2.25 dB mask on the AOI-01 zoom only.
tiers.max_confidence: low unless the T2 skill condition in t2_skill_bar passes
tiers.class_behaviour: Binding E with reason low_confidence when low. The would-be class is shown only in the Studio verification queue, with a mandatory skill caption.
tiers.display: Amber chip: Own model candidate: verify before action. Command shows E: monitor and verify (own unqualified detector).

tiers.name: Agency, dated
tiers.admission: An agency extent whose acquisition is within +/-3 days of the case reference date: GISTDA ALOS-2 15 Sep or AIT 14 Sep only if permission is granted (reference 15 Sep); the 4009 22 Oct layer for its own dated case (reference 22 Oct).
tiers.display: Blue chip: Agency flood map (source, date), used as provided; unvalidated; planning class, not a warning.

tiers.name: Qualified
tiers.admission: Human-reviewed dated reference, frozen hold-out, calibration and label receipt. Not pursued in this release.
tiers.display: Locked chip: Not reached in this release, beside the eight section 3.6.6 gates with status.

invariants_at_every_tier: accepted_fpps and accepted_action_class are null below T4.
No class above E without derived medium confidence, or a declared scenario confidence in the SCN lanes.
The temporal honesty assertion in guardrails holds.
evidence_tier_model.no_assumed_components_in_obs_or_scn: No FPPS component is assumed at 0, 50 or 100 in the OBS or SCN lanes. Assumed completions exist only as T1 assumed-completion arithmetic and are labelled as such (plan 1.2).
evidence_tier_model.no_assumed_components_status: Drafter reading DR-A05. Plan 1.2 forbids assumed components in 'the OBS or SCN lanes' and, in the next sentence, keeps assumed completions as T1 arithmetic; T1 is the scenario tier. The draft reads this as: no case row and no scenario cell in OBS, SCN or SCN-ENV carries an assumed component; assumed-completion arithmetic is a separate table, labelled as such, and is never a case row or a scenario cell. An earlier draft narrowed the rule to 'OBS or SCN-ENV'; the plan's wording is restored here. The owners confirm or amend the reading at signing.

date_rule.rule: An input is event_aligned only when its acquisition is within +/-3 days of the case reference date. The rule is strict: nothing passes it automatically.

accumulated_layer.reason: No per-patch dates, Field_Validation=0, and a span from 1 Aug 2024 into October 2024. It fails the recency condition.
accumulated_layer.date_span_status: Drafter reading DR-A10. The layer name gives 1 Aug to 12 Oct 2024. Plan 0 item 1 says the union spans 1 Aug to 22 Oct and plan 4.1 says '1 Aug-12/22 Oct'; the decision log calls it the Aug-Oct accumulated layer. The draft records the layer name as it is in the package. Whichever end date is right, the layer is a season window and fails the recency condition. The owners confirm at signing.

layer_22_oct.temporal_relation_scope: Case O2 only (reference date 22 Oct 2024). Against a September reference date (cases O1 and O4) the same layer is dated_other.
layer_22_oct.label: late-season residual water, 22 Oct 2024
layer_22_oct.not: It is not a lower level of the September flood and is never described as one.

date_rule.flood_uncertainty_axis: Built only from perturbations of a single product state: minus, as-provided, plus one pixel. No flood level is labelled central.

confidence_rule_v1.rights_note: Rights are not an input to confidence. They drive publication_eligibility (guardrail 6).
confidence_rule_v1.high: Requires T4. Never assigned in this release.

medium_requires_all.condition: Tier T3, or tier T2 passing the skill condition in t2_skill_bar.
Acquisition within +/-3 days of the case reference date.
medium_requires_all.note: The season-window 4009 union fails. In SCN lanes this condition is replaced by the scenario declaration and the row is labelled scenario.

medium_requires_all.condition: Unit valid coverage inside the product footprint or analysis extent is at least 0.80.
medium_requires_all.note: For 4009 in Mae Sai this is satisfied by construction (the analysis extent covers all eight tambons) and is reported as by_construction.

medium_requires_all.condition: The absolute difference between exposure with the flood input grown by one pixel and shrunk by one pixel is at most 15 points. For T2 the abstention fraction must also be at most 0.20.
All five components computed, none assumed.

medium_requires_all.note: A unit below this threshold also falls under guardrail GR1, which decides the class. See guardrails GR1_minimum_denominators.precedence.

medium_requires_all.condition: Baseline vehicle connected-no-route share is at most 10 percent.
At least one hospital is reachable at baseline.

scenario_rows.applies_to: Tier T1 rows (lanes SCN and SCN-ENV).
plan_text: Plan 3.3, tier table, T1 maximum confidence: 'scenario confidence' (rule v1 with the recency condition replaced by the scenario declaration).
Plan 3.3, rule v1, condition 1: Tier T3, or T2 passing the skill condition.
Plan 3.3, invariants: no class above E without derived medium (or declared scenario) confidence.
scenario_rows.gap: Read literally, condition C1 fails for every T1 row, so every SE1, SE2 and S1-S9 scenario row is low confidence and class E. That contradicts the case design in plan 6, which expects scenario classes above E. The plan does not say how C1 applies to a T1 row, and it calls scenario confidence both derived and declared.
rule: Scenario confidence is derived, not declared. It is rule v1 with two substitutions.

C1 is evaluated on the base flood input of the scenario. It is satisfied, and recorded as by_scenario_declaration, when the base input is an agency product used as provided: the 4009 accumulated layer for SCN-ENV rows, and the 4009 22 Oct layer for scenario cells built on O2. It fails when the base input is an own T2 candidate that does not pass the T2 skill condition.
C2 is replaced by the scenario declaration and recorded as by_scenario_declaration.
C3 to C8 are evaluated exactly as for an observed row.

The row carries confidence_class medium or low, because the scoring module accepts only high, medium and low, together with confidence_kind scenario. It is displayed as scenario confidence and is never shown or counted as observed confidence.
scenario_rows.rule_status: Drafter reading DR-A07, not in the plan. This is the most outcome-sensitive reading in this file: it decides whether any scenario row can have a class above E. The owners confirm it, or replace it with one of the alternatives, before signing.
alternatives: Literal: C1 fails for every T1 row and every scenario class is E.
Declared: each scenario cell states its confidence in v1b, and C1 to C8 are not evaluated for it.

confidence_rule_v1.basis_record: Every row records pass, fail, by_construction or by_scenario_declaration for each condition and lists failed_conditions. The value by_scenario_declaration exists only under drafter reading DR-A07.

t2_skill_bar.rule: A T2 input is low confidence unless all four conditions pass.
t2_skill_bar.consequence: T2 never yields a binding class above E unless the condition passes.
t2_skill_bar.metric_wording: The GEOID figure is agreement with a same-pass CEMS map. It is not independent accuracy.
t2_skill_bar.exploratory_note: The 0.40 bar was written after an exploratory all-tile figure of 0.455 had been seen. See disclosure item EK-06.

geoid_split.dataset: GEOID-Flood sample, activation EMSR712-3, 29 Sentinel-1 GRD tiles (pre 2023-09-08, post 2024-01-03)
geoid_split.rule: Sort the 29 tile IDs in ascending numeric order. The first 15 are development tiles. The remaining 14 are test tiles.
geoid_split.rule_status: Drafter reading DR-A01. The plan says 29 tiles by tile ID, 15 dev / 14 test, and gives no list. This ordering rule is the drafting agent's reading. The owners confirm or amend it at signing.

uses.M1-literal: Run once on all tiles and reported by split. No tuning.
uses.M1-v2: Tuned on development tiles only, then fixed with a config SHA before any Mae Sai run. Target date in the plan: Wed 7 Oct 2026.
uses.A6-prime: Trained and calibrated on development tiles, tested on test tiles, applied to Mae Sai as report-only.

limits: One foreign event; the split is spatial, by tile.
Test tiles were included in an earlier exploratory all-tile diagnostic and are disclosed as previously seen.
CEMS labels come from the same pass, so the comparison is never called independent.
The GEOID sample has no DEM, HAND or slope layer. M1-v2 is fixed slope-free on GEOID and the HAND/slope mask is applied on Mae Sai as a disclosed difference.

Design choices were informed by the Mae Sai diagnosis. Test tiles had been included in an earlier exploratory all-tile diagnostic (0.161 to 0.455), which is labelled exploratory.

scoring_frame.signed_decision_text: D4: Freeze score scaling. The flood anchor is 0.20; the team discloses that it was chosen after seeing the data, and 0.10 and 0.30 run as sensitivity checks. Exposure is share-based. Vulnerability uses national P10/P90 anchors. Permanent water comes from WorldCover. Outcome: Adopted, with the disclosure.
scoring_frame.formula: FPPS = sum over the five components of weight x component, each component on 0-100, rounded to 2 decimals
scoring_frame.normalisation: Absolute, declared anchors. No batch scaling and no max-normalisation (guardrail 2).

flood_likelihood_0_100.definition: 100 x min(1, flooded share of the unit's non-permanent-water land / anchor)
flood_likelihood_0_100.anchor_disclosure: The 0.20 anchor was declared after the 0.05 anchor was seen to saturate in 5 of 8 Mae Sai tambons, as stated in plan 3.4. It was chosen after seeing the data. The per-tambon envelope shares kept from that analysis show 6 of the 8 above 0.05, not 5. The owners check the count and correct this sentence before signing.
flood_likelihood_0_100.anchor_disclosure_status: Drafter reading DR-A11. The count is quoted from plan 3.4 and does not match the retained shares (disclosure items EK-05 and EK-R3). The disclosure itself, that 0.20 was chosen after seeing the data, is not in doubt.

permanent_water.sensitivity_note: JRC Global Surface Water is reported as a sensitivity note only.

exposure_0_100.definition: 100 x residents whose population cell centre is inside the flood extent / unit residents
exposure_0_100.population_vintage_axis: 2024/2020 1 km rescale, as an ensemble axis. The plan gives no formula; it is open item OI-13 in v1b.
exposure_0_100.note: Same semantics as src/floodguard/evidence_flood_scenario.py (cell-centre rule). A density anchor is rejected because it is independent of the flood.

access_gap_0_100.definition: Baseline-access-weighted mean of newly-lost access shares, counted only for people who had access at baseline

road_criticality_0_100.definition: 100 x residents with a baseline route to any hospital or main road who lose all routes / those residents
road_criticality_0_100.note: A network-consequence measure. The plan notes that this definition makes an isolation-driven class B reachable; see disclosure item EK-01.

vulnerability_context_0_100.definition: 100 x clip((dependent share - lower anchor) / (upper anchor - lower anchor), 0, 1), where dependent share is residents aged 0-14 plus residents aged 60 and over, divided by all residents
vulnerability_context_0_100.anchor_values_status: Not computed. They are computed once in v1b from the national tambon distribution of the WorldPop 2024 1 km dependent share, before any case scoring. This file never carries the values; they are recorded in planning_protocol_v1b.json.

terrain_remoteness_proxy.reason: The local DEM does not cover Rim Kok.
terrain_remoteness_proxy.definition: Not defined in the plan. The definition and its anchor are open item OI-12 in v1b.

vulnerability_context_0_100.source: WorldPop Global2 R2025A v1, 2024, 1 km constrained age counts
vulnerability_context_0_100.caveat: Modelled 1 km age composition applied to 2020 100 m counts; not observed; within-cell composition assumed uniform.

leave_one_component_out.rule: For each of the five components, report an FPPS with that component's weight set to 0 and the other four weights renormalised to sum to 1, and the v1 class of that FPPS.
leave_one_component_out.rule_status: Drafter reading DR-A02. The plan requires a leave-one-component-out FPPS and class on every row and does not say how the remaining weights are treated. Renormalisation follows scoring.validate_weights. The owners confirm or amend it at signing.

weight_presets.note: Non-default presets are normalised to sum to 1 by the scorer. The default is the published default. A user re-weighted view is labelled user-weighted view, not the published default. Weight presets are never cut.

scoring_frame.lane_disclosure: One flood input drives 4 of 5 components (90% of weight). This sentence appears on the overlay and in the brief appendix.

class_rules.signed_decision_text: D6: v1 class rules stay binding, and v2 is reported as a predeclared secondary axis.

v1.evaluation: Rules are evaluated in the order listed. The first rule that matches gives the class.

reason_codes.low_confidence: Monitor and obtain better evidence before action.
reason_codes.low_priority_score: Lower relative priority. This is not a safety statement.

added_reason_code.insufficient_denominator: A unit with fewer than 100 residents gets no class (guardrail 1). This is the only reason code the planning overlay adds.

v1.would_be_class: For low-confidence rows the scorer is rerun with confidence set to medium. The result is never binding. It is shown in the Studio verification queue, and in Command only for T3 rows that are low because of a non-evidence condition, with the failed condition named.

v2.implements: Proposal section 5.2 triggers, as a wrapper around v1.

triggers.A: v1 gives A AND the unit's dependent-share concentration is at or above the national P75.
triggers.B: A top-20 critical link inside the flood extent isolates at least 500 residents of the unit.
triggers.C: FPPS is at least 35 AND confidence is medium or scenario AND an OSM hospital or a uniquely located DDPM shelter serving the unit is inside the extent or loses all vehicle routes.
triggers.D: FPPS is at least 35 AND the recurrence flag is set. The flag uses GISTDA Repeated Flood Areas if obtained; otherwise JRC occurrence of at least 25 percent outside permanent water. Being inside both 4009 layers does not count, because that is the same season.
triggers.E: Low confidence OR exposure below 10 OR FPPS below 35.

evaluation.rule: Triggers are evaluated in the order E, A, B, C, D. The first trigger that matches gives the v2 class.
evaluation.otherwise_meaning: A unit with FPPS of at least 35, exposure of at least 10 and medium or scenario confidence that meets none of A to D gets no v2 letter. It is reported as 'no v2 trigger met', counted as its own category, and counted as a class change against v1 in the v1 / v2 comparison.
evaluation.rule_status: Drafter reading DR-A08, not in the plan. The plan lists the five triggers with no order and no fallback, so a unit where both the B and the C trigger fire, or one where none fires, has no defined v2 class. E is placed first because of the invariant that no class above E exists without medium or scenario confidence; A to D then follow the v1 order. The owners confirm or amend it at signing.
alternatives: When no trigger matches, fall back to the v1 class.
When no trigger matches, fall back to D.
When no trigger matches, fall back to E.

v2.reason_code_mapping: v2 triggers map to the existing essential_service_access reason code plus a trigger_evidence field. No new reason code is added for v2.
depends_on_v1b: the definitions of 'isolates', 'serving the unit' and the unit-level recurrence flag (v1b class_rule_v2_inputs, open item OI-18)
recurrence layer (GISTDA Repeated Flood Areas if obtained, otherwise JRC occurrence)

class_rules.because_v1_is_binding: CLAIMS.md and the Q&A bank carry a table: Where our class rules approximate section 5.2.

guardrails.rule: A unit with fewer than 100 residents gets no class (insufficient_denominator). A ratio requires at least 50 people per group.
guardrails.precedence: GR1 decides the class, ahead of confidence condition C6. A unit with fewer than 100 residents has no binding class (reason insufficient_denominator), no would-be class and no v2 class. Its confidence is still recorded as low, with C6 in failed_conditions.
guardrails.precedence_status: Drafter reading DR-A09, not in the plan. Plan 2.3 item 1 says such a unit gets no class. Plan 3.3 condition 6 makes it low confidence, which the v1 rule turns into class E. Plan 5 item 10 lists 'denominator' among the non-evidence conditions for which a would-be class is shown in Command. The owners confirm which of these applies.

enforcement.note: To be enforced by planning_assessment.py and verify_planning_assessment.py (plan task E8). Neither exists on this lineage. Required before any scoring.

guardrails.rule: The planning verifier must reject batch-scaled components. The planning frame uses its own anchor version IDs, to be declared in a new docs/model_contract.md section 2c; section 2b's density exposure and fpps_flood_anchor_v1 apply to the GeoAI runner only.

enforcement.note: verify_planning_assessment.py and docs/model_contract.md section 2c do not exist on this lineage. Required before any scoring.

guardrails.rule: The five components of a row come from one flood input, one routing context and one closure rule. The planning verifier must check the input hashes. The overlay discloses that one flood input drives 4 of 5 components (90% of weight).

enforcement.note: The verifier and its input-hash check do not exist on this lineage. Required before any scoring.

guardrails.rule: The product that drives a lane may not be the agreement reference for any detector in that lane. Cross-input comparison is symmetric divergence only.

enforcement.note: A rule for how comparisons are designed. No automated check exists. Required before the divergence study A5.

guardrails.rule: Context, access and closure builds may run before v1b is in force. No FPPS, no A-E class and no ensemble may be computed for any real unit until the signed v1b's SHA-256 is recorded in RECEIPTS.jsonl. The grid, nodes, links, anchors and case list are fixed before any scoring.
guardrails.rule_status: Drafter reading DR-A06. Plan 2.3 item 5 forbids computing any FPPS, class or ensemble before the v1b receipt, with no qualifier. The words 'for any real unit' were added by the drafting agent because the existing test suite scores synthetic fixtures on every run (tests/test_scoring.py). The reading does not excuse the replay computation of 28 Sep 2026, which scored real tambons after the plan date; that is disclosed in item EK-R1. The owners confirm or amend the wording at signing.
guardrails.status_at_drafting: No FPPS, class or ensemble was computed while drafting or revising this file. One computation for real tambons was made after the plan date on another lineage; see known_departure.
guardrails.known_departure: Disclosure item EK-R1: scenario FPPS and score-implied classes for the eight Mae Sai tambons were computed on the replay lineage on 28 Sep 2026, two days after the plan adopted this rule.

enforcement.note: tests/test_planning_protocol.py checks that the two protocol files state no score, class or component value for a real unit outside the disclosure, and that no receipt names a draft. Nothing technical stops a script from computing a score: the rule binds people and agents.

guardrails.rule: publication_eligibility is local, pitch or public, set at write time and separate from confidence. An overlay's rights level is the minimum across its lineage. Only public overlays may be written to apps/web/public/. evidence_catalog._POLICY is not edited.

enforcement.note: rights.py and the verifier's public-write check do not exist on this lineage. Required before any overlay is written under apps/web/public/.

guardrails.rule: No row whose temporal_relation is not event_aligned may carry the label OBS together with a binding class above E.

enforcement.note: To be asserted by the verifier. Required before any scoring.

guardrails.rule: A class is headlined only if it keeps at least 60 percent retention over the single-state ensemble. Otherwise it is shown as unstable: verify.
guardrails.fallback_text: no class met the stability rule; shown as unstable: verify

enforcement.note: To be applied by uncertainty_ensemble.py (plan task E10). Required before any class is headlined.

guardrails.rule: A pre-commit test must fail if any committed script reads AIT-VAP001 or MBRSC paths without a recorded grant receipt. No AIT or MBRSC number appears in committed code or on any public surface.

enforcement.note: No pre-commit or CI test of this kind exists on this lineage. The existing AIT tests check the processing_allowed=false invariant of the AIT candidate record only. Required with plan task A1.

equity_statement_rule.ratio_null_when: Fewer than 50 people in either group, or both rates are 0. A reason code is recorded.
equity_statement_rule.gap_sentence_requires: Bounds that exclude zero AND at least 60 percent sign retention across the ensemble.
equity_statement_rule.otherwise_fixed_sentence: no age-group gap distinguishable from zero under the tested assumptions

exploratory_knowledge_disclosure.statement: This protocol was written after exploratory analysis. The items below are results the team had already seen that could have informed a rule. Several include scores or classes for the real Mae Sai tambons. The rules are therefore not blind to outcomes, and no output of this protocol may be described as preregistered or confirmatory.
exploratory_knowledge_disclosure.completeness: Listed by the drafting agent from the plan, the plan-session scratchpad, this lineage and the items the owner supplied for the replay lineage. The signers add anything else they have seen before signing.

flag_definitions.real_tambon_scores_or_classes_seen: True when an FPPS or an A-E class (binding, would-be or score-implied) for a real tambon was seen, or when a cited source computes one.
flag_definitions.real_tambon_component_values_seen: True when a value of one of the five components, or of the share that feeds it directly, was seen for a real tambon.
flag_definitions.guard_status: protocol_rule: the guard is a rule declared in this protocol; it binds later work and nothing checks it automatically yet. control_missing: the guard also names a test, verifier, annotation or retirement that does not exist on this lineage; guard_gaps lists what is missing, and it must be in place before any scoring.

items.title: Gap-1 external-extent chains (old chain) for the eight Mae Sai tambons
items.what_was_seen: Exploratory closure, routing, component and scorer runs for the eight Mae Sai tambons under three external extents (the 4009 accumulated layer, the 4009 22 Oct layer and the AIT 14 Sep extent), three destination sets and four normalisation frames (absolute share, density anchor, district max-normalised, pooled max-normalised), with confidence assumed medium and missing components completed at 0, 50 and 100. FPPS values and A-E classes for the real tambons were seen. The plan summarises the envelope result as: under an absolute frame the accumulated envelope gives B, D and E (Ko Chang isolation), and A and C appeared only through max-normalisation artefacts. The chain read the AIT extent before any permission decision; no AIT-derived result is recorded in this file (guardrail GR9). Those results exist only in the uncommitted scratch files.

items.could_bias: Frames and component definitions could have been chosen because they give a fuller spread of classes, or because they keep a known tambon in a known class.
items.guard: Every cell of every case is reported whatever it shows. Scenario and engine classes are never counted as observed. The class coverage table is reported per lane, observed first. Leave-one-component-out and the 0.10/0.30 anchor runs are reported for every row. v1 class thresholds are the unchanged code. The old-chain numbers are not reused: every value is recomputed under this protocol after v1b is in force.
guard_gaps: No verifier exists yet to check that every cell is reported and that scenario and engine classes are kept out of the observed column (plan task E8).

items.title: Hat Yai closure-threshold sweep
items.what_was_seen: On the Hat Yai AOI-03 candidate, which is case H1, closed-segment counts and newly lost hospital access at 15, 30 and 60 minutes were computed for walking and modelled-vehicle modes under four closure rules: any positive overlap, at least 20 m, at least 50 m, and at least 20 m with mapped bridges and tunnels left open. Walking 30-minute loss fell from about 9,940 residents under any overlap to about 6,825 at 20 m and about 374 at 50 m; modelled-vehicle loss fell from about 23,105 to about 11,100 and about 2,128. The committed note concludes that the consequence figure is not robust to the closure-length assumption. No FPPS or class was computed.

items.title: Scenario FPPS and score-implied classes for all eight Mae Sai tambons on the replay (pre-D4 anchors)
items.what_was_seen: Commit 2e5a099 (branch claude/mae-sai-fpps-priority-playbook, 28 Sep 2026) computed scenario FPPS for all eight Mae Sai tambons on the r2 reconstruction with pre-D4 anchors (replay_fpps_anchor_v1: flood 0.25, exposure share plus a 5,000-person headcount, terrain proxy 0.25). The scores ran from 89.34 down to 31.27. The binding class of every tambon was E, by the low-confidence rule. The same commit also reran the class rule at medium confidence and showed the result for each tambon as a 'score implies' class: apps/web/src/lib/replay-fpps.ts sets score_implied_class, mae-sai-priority-card.tsx renders it with the playbook of that class, and replay-fpps.test.ts asserts that the top-ranked tambon's implied class is one of A to D. So the team has seen would-be A-D classes for real Mae Sai tambons under the v1 thresholds. This file does not record which class each tambon was shown; the signers add it if they recall it. The computation is dated 28 Sep 2026, two days after the plan (26 Sep 2026) adopted the rule that no FPPS, class or ensemble is computed before the v1b receipt. It was made on the replay lineage, outside the planning tier, and it is recorded here as a departure from that rule. The eight scores, each with class E, are shown on the /policy/ page on master as a superseded historical example; the score-implied classes are not shown there. All of this was seen before v1a and v1b.
